Plot a comparison of transitions between groups

Source: R/plot-comparison.R
plot.lsa_comparison.Rd

plot() draws the result of compare_lsa() or bayes_compare_lsa() as a barrel chart (default) or a heatmap. When the same states are observed in two or more groups, a comparison shows which transitions differ between them, by how much, and whether the difference is larger than chance, so a display of it has to show both the transitions themselves in each group and the test of their difference.

The barrel is a back-to-back chart with one row per transition: the first group's bar runs to the left and the second's to the right, bar length is the transition probability (or count), bar colour is the log odds ratio of the transition within the group (blue over-represented, red avoided), and the centre shows the p-value of the difference, in bold when significant. The rows are the top_n most frequent transitions, or with rank = "effect" those with the strongest association in either group. The heatmap draws the difference between the groups as a grid of from by to states. With more than two groups, each pair is drawn as a facet.

The tested differences are read as a table with transitions(cmp). To colour the ribbons of a chord diagram by a group difference, see plot_chords().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'lsa_comparison'
plot(
  x,
  style = c("barrel", "heatmap"),
  value = c("prob", "count"),
  rank = c("frequency", "effect"),
  top_n = 12L,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_comparison_pairwise'
plot(
  x,
  style = c("barrel", "heatmap"),
  value = c("prob", "count"),
  rank = c("frequency", "effect"),
  top_n = 12L,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

The result of compare_lsa() or bayes_compare_lsa().

style

"barrel" (default) or "heatmap".

value

For the barrel, bar length: "prob" (default) or "count".

rank

For the barrel, which transitions to show: "frequency" (default, the most frequent overall) or "effect" (the strongest association, largest absolute log odds ratio, in either group).

top_n

For the barrel, the number of transitions shown (default 12); with several pairs the same transitions are shown in every facet.

...

Ignored.

Value

A ggplot object, drawn when printed.

See also

compare_lsa(), bayes_compare_lsa(), transitions(), plot_chords()

Examples

gfit <- lsa(group_regulation_long, actor = "Actor", action = "Action",
            time = "Time", group = "Achiever")
set.seed(1)
cmp <- compare_lsa(gfit, R = 100, adjust = "BH")
plot(cmp)

plot(cmp, rank = "effect")

plot(cmp, style = "heatmap")
